questions.stem: With reference to the size of the Council of Ministers in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The size of the Council of Ministers in Jammu and Kashmir is capped at 10% of the total membership of its Legislative Assembly, a ceiling similar to the one applicable to the Government of NCT of Delhi.
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, which caps the size of a State's Council of Ministers at 15% of Assembly strength, applies uniformly to Jammu and Kashmir as well.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: under Section 54 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the Council of Ministers of the Union Territory cannot exceed 10% of Assembly strength, similar to the cap under the GNCTD Act for Delhi. Statement 2 is wrong because Article 164(1A), inserted by the 91st Amendment, applies the 15% cap only to full States; J&K, being a Union Territory with a legislature, is instead governed by the special statutory ceiling in its Reorganisation Act, which is why its Council of Ministers hit its 'maximum permissible statutory limit of nine' after the recent expansion.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Dissident National Conference MLAs meet Omar, Farooq to air grievances
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 164(1A)/91st Amendment cap on Council of Ministers size versus the distinct statutory cap for Union Territories with legislatures.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Exploration Licence (EL) and critical mineral block auctions in India. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Exploration Licence (EL) is a mineral concession introduced by the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023.
An Exploration Licence permits the holder to also carry out mining operations without obtaining a separate mining lease.
Under the MMDR Amendment Act, 2023, the power to auction blocks of critical and strategic minerals vests exclusively with the State Governments.
Graphite and rare earth elements are among the minerals notified as critical and strategic minerals for auction.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the EL was indeed introduced by the 2023 amendment, and the ninth tranche of auctions explicitly includes graphite and rare earth elements among the offered blocks. Statement 2 is wrong because an EL covers only reconnaissance and prospecting; actual mining still requires a separate mining lease or composite licence. Statement 3 is wrong because the 2023 amendment empowered the Central Government, not the States, to auction blocks of specified critical and strategic minerals.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Mines Ministry launches ninth round of auctions, offers 20 critical mineral blocks
questions.pyqLink: Tests the MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 and the critical minerals list — a recurring prelims theme since 2023-24.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding noise pollution regulation in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Under these rules, the permissible ambient noise level in a residential area during the day is higher than during the night.
The Central Pollution Control Board classifies an area as a 'silence zone' if it falls within 100 metres of a hospital, educational institution or court.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 derive their authority from the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; ambient standards prescribe lower permissible decibel limits at night than during the day across all zone categories; and the 100-metre radius around hospitals, educational institutions and courts is the statutory definition of a silence zone, within which stricter limits and a ban on loudspeakers/horns apply.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: A noisy Anthropocene is imposing fatal stress on wildlife
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 and CPCB zone classification, triggered by the Science study on noise stress on wildlife.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding space debris. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: Space debris includes defunct satellites, spent rocket stages and fragments generated by collisions or anti-satellite (ASAT) tests.
The Kessler Syndrome describes a scenario where debris density in a given orbital regime is high enough to trigger a self-sustaining cascade of collisions.
ISRO's System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management (IS4OM) is its dedicated centre for space situational awareness and collision-avoidance analysis.
The Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC) functions as a specialized agency of the United Nations tasked with space debris mitigation.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct descriptions of space debris, the Kessler Syndrome, and ISRO's IS4OM, which is the context behind the new private debris-recovery facility. Statement 4 is wrong: the IADC is an independent international forum of space agencies that coordinates on debris issues, not a UN-constituted specialized agency; debris mitigation guidelines at the UN level instead come through COPUOS.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Hyderabad startup opens India's first private space debris recovery facility
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of orbital debris and the Kessler Syndrome, triggered by India's first private debris-recovery facility.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of dams/projects and the rivers on which they are built. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Bhakra Dam and Pandoh Dam are correctly matched: Bhakra Dam is built on the Sutlej River, and Pandoh Dam, part of the Beas-Sutlej Link project, is on the Beas River. Pong Dam is incorrectly matched — it is also on the Beas River, not the Ravi. Nangal Dam, located downstream of Bhakra as part of the Bhakra-Nangal project, is on the Sutlej River, not the Ravi, so that pair is also wrong.

questions.stem: With reference to the PM Internship Scheme, which one of the following best describes it?
options: A scheme run by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship providing stipendiary apprenticeships to ITI graduates, funded entirely through the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
A scheme administered by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to give India's youth a one-year internship with top companies, combining a central government stipend with an industry contribution
A Ministry of Labour and Employment initiative providing wage subsidies to first-time formal-sector employees under the Employment Linked Incentive scheme
A NITI Aayog programme mandating public sector undertakings to reserve board-level internship positions for engineering graduates
questions.explanation: The PM Internship Scheme, announced in the Union Budget for FY25, is run by the corporate affairs ministry to place youth in internships with top companies, with the stipend jointly funded by the Centre and participating companies; it aims at 10 million internships over five years. Option 1 confuses it with the Ministry of Skill Development's apprenticeship schemes, option 3 with the Employment Linked Incentive scheme, and option 4 is fabricated.

questions.sourceTitle: Internship scheme's new pilot gets more takers post rejig

questions.stem:
Statement-I: Indian banks' treasury income fell sharply in the September 2026 quarter even though they continued to hold government bonds.
Statement-II: Bond prices and bond yields move inversely, so a rise in government bond yields causes mark-to-market losses on a bank's bond investment portfolio.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct, and Statement-II is the precise mechanism behind Statement-I: a rise in government bond yields reduces the market price of existing bonds, forcing banks to book mark-to-market losses on their investment portfolios (as seen in SBI's and PNB's reported treasury income declines), which directly explains the fall in treasury income.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Bond yield rise squeezes banks' Q2 treasury gains
questions.pyqLink: Tests the inverse bond price-yield relationship and MTM accounting for bank investment portfolios, a core monetary economics concept.

questions.stem: The UPSC recently declared the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 result. With reference to the constitutional provisions governing the Union Public Service Commission, consider the following statements: 1. The Chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India. 2. A member of the UPSC can be removed by the President on the ground of misbehaviour only after the Supreme Court, on a reference made to it, holds an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed. 3. The term of office of a member of the UPSC is six years or till the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier. 4. The annual report of the UPSC is submitted to the Governor of the State concerned. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India.

A member of the UPSC can be removed by the President on the ground of misbehaviour only after the Supreme Court, on a reference made to it, holds an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed.
The term of office of a member of the UPSC is six years or till the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier.
The annual report of the UPSC is submitted to the Governor of the State concerned.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Article 316 vests appointment in the President, and Article 317 requires a Supreme Court inquiry before removal for misbehaviour. Statement 3 is wrong — a Union Commission member's term is six years or till age 65 (62 is the State PSC age limit, a near-miss distractor). Statement 4 is wrong — under Article 323, the Union Commission's report is submitted to the President, not a Governor (State Commissions report to the Governor).
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: UPSC Mains Result 2026 declared: Here's how to check
questions.pyqLink: Tests Articles 315-323 on UPSC composition, tenure and removal — similar to UPSC 2017/2021 questions on constitutional bodies' appointment and removal procedure.

questions.stem: Delhi's air quality has slipped into the 'severe' category, prompting invocation of Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). Consider the following statements about GRAP: 1. GRAP is implemented in the National Capital Region and is based on Air Quality Index (AQI) categories notified by the CPCB. 2. GRAP has four stages, with Stage IV invoked when the AQI enters the 'Severe+' category. 3. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) is the statutory body responsible for enforcing GRAP. 4. GRAP was first notified under the provisions of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: GRAP is implemented in the National Capital Region and is based on Air Quality Index (AQI) categories notified by the CPCB.
GRAP has four stages, with Stage IV invoked when the AQI enters the 'Severe+' category.
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) is the statutory body responsible for enforcing GRAP.
GRAP was first notified under the provisions of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: GRAP's four stages (Poor, Very Poor, Severe, Severe+) are AQI-linked and enforced by the CAQM, a statutory body created under the CAQM Act, 2021. Statement 4 is wrong — GRAP was first notified in 2016 on the Supreme Court's directive under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, not the Air Act, 1981 (a near-miss distractor, since the Air Act deals with pollution control boards generally).
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
questions.pyqLink: Tests GRAP and CAQM, a recurring current-environment-governance topic; similar to UPSC's past questions on statutory pollution-control bodies and their enabling Acts.

questions.stem: Asian tech stocks fell sharply amid fears of tighter AI regulation and rising borrowing costs in the US. With reference to the relationship between interest rates and financial markets, consider the following statements: 1. A rise in benchmark interest rates increases the cost of borrowing for companies and typically exerts downward pressure on equity market valuations. 2. In India, the inflation target of 4% (with a band of +/- 2%) is set and pursued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the amended RBI Act. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A rise in benchmark interest rates increases the cost of borrowing for companies and typically exerts downward pressure on equity market valuations.
In India, the inflation target of 4% (with a band of +/- 2%) is set and pursued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the amended RBI Act.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — higher rates raise discount rates on future earnings and borrowing costs, depressing equity valuations, which is the mechanism behind the sell-off described. Statement 2 is incorrect because the flexible inflation-targeting framework (4% +/- 2%) is operated by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, not SEBI, which is the securities market regulator, a classic wrong-institution distractor.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Tech firms suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
questions.pyqLink: Tests the monetary policy transmission mechanism and institutional mandate of the RBI's MPC, a recurring UPSC Economy theme (e.g., UPSC 2021 RBI expansionary policy question).

questions.stem: The Supreme Court has agreed to hear an election petition arising from a one-vote victory margin in a Tamil Nadu assembly constituency. With reference to the adjudication of election disputes in India, consider the following statements: 1. An election petition challenging the result of a Lok Sabha or State Assembly election can be filed directly before the Supreme Court if the winning margin is less than ten votes. 2. An election petition can be filed only before the High Court having jurisdiction over the constituency, as provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. 3. An appeal against the decision of a High Court in an election petition lies directly to the Supreme Court under Section 116A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: An election petition challenging the result of a Lok Sabha or State Assembly election can be filed directly before the Supreme Court if the winning margin is less than ten votes.
An election petition can be filed only before the High Court having jurisdiction over the constituency, as provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
An appeal against the decision of a High Court in an election petition lies directly to the Supreme Court under Section 116A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is false — there is no margin-based exception; Article 329(b) bars interference with elections except by an election petition, which under Sections 80 and 81 of the RP Act, 1951 must always be filed before the High Court, regardless of the winning margin, exactly the route the Madras High Court took here. Statement 2 is correct per Sections 80/81, and Statement 3 is correct since Section 116A gives a direct statutory right of appeal to the Supreme Court, which is why the apex court could admit this appeal.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Supreme Court agrees to hear DMK leader's plea challenging rejection of election petition
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 329 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951 on election dispute resolution, similar in spirit to UPSC's past questions on the Election Commission's and judiciary's roles in electoral disputes.

questions.stem: With reference to drug and public-health regulation in India, as illustrated by the recent Maharashtra FDA enforcement drive and the NDPS-related arrests, consider the following pairs: 1. World Health Organization (WHO) — Declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for outbreaks of international significance 2. Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) — Sole authority responsible for granting licences for the manufacture and sale of all drugs and cosmetics within every State 3. Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 — Governs offences related to illegal manufacture, possession and trafficking of narcotic drugs 4. State Food and Drug Administration — State-level authority responsible for issuing and cancelling licences for drug and cosmetic establishments under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for outbreaks of international significance
Sole authority responsible for granting licences for the manufacture and sale of all drugs and cosmetics within every State
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
Governs offences related to illegal manufacture, possession and trafficking of narcotic drugs
State-level authority responsible for issuing and cancelling licences for drug and cosmetic establishments under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched: WHO declares PHEICs, the NDPS Act, 1985 governs narcotics offences (the basis for the NDPS arrests in Maharashtra), and State FDAs — as the Maharashtra FDA did by cancelling 122 licences — license and regulate establishments under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Pair 2 is wrong because CDSCO regulates only specific categories (new drugs, biologicals, large-volume parenterals, clinical trials) under the central government, while licensing of most drug sales and manufacturing establishments within a State is done by the State Drug Control/FDA, not CDSCO alone.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Centre-State division of drug regulatory authority under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and CDSCO's mandate, akin to UPSC's institutional-detail pairs questions on regulatory bodies.

questions.stem: Delhi's air quality worsens every winter due to 'meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature,' which trap pollutants near the surface. Which one of the following best describes the atmospheric phenomenon primarily responsible for this trapping effect?
options: The Coriolis effect, which slows down surface winds over northern India during the winter months
The urban heat island effect, in which cities are significantly warmer than surrounding rural areas, drawing pollutants inward
Orographic lifting caused by the Himalayas, which forces pollutant-laden air to rise and disperse over the plains
Temperature inversion, in which a layer of warmer air sits above cooler surface air and prevents vertical mixing, trapping pollutants near the ground
questions.explanation: Temperature inversion is the correct mechanism: in winter, the ground cools faster than the air above it, creating a warm layer aloft that acts as a lid, preventing pollutants from dispersing upward — exactly the 'lower wind speed and drop in temperature' effect described. The Coriolis effect governs wind deflection due to Earth's rotation, not local calm conditions; the urban heat island effect concerns temperature differences between cities and their surroundings, not pollutant trapping; and orographic lifting would disperse, not trap, pollutants.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: As New Delhi's air turns toxic again, people complain of unaffordable air purification products
questions.pyqLink: Tests the climatology concept of temperature inversion behind winter smog in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, a classic static-geography anchor for recurring Delhi pollution news.

questions.stem: Andhra Pradesh has stepped up health surveillance at three airports as Ebola spreads faster than previous outbreaks. Statement-I: India has intensified health surveillance for Ebola at select international airports as part of its public health preparedness obligations. Statement-II: As a WHO member state, India is bound by the International Health Regulations (IHR), 2005, which require designated airports and ports to maintain capacities for screening and managing public health risks posed by international travellers. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct and confirmed by the article's description of airport screening readiness. Statement-II correctly explains it: the IHR, 2005, binding on WHO member states under Article 21 of the WHO Constitution, obligate countries to build core surveillance and response capacities at designated points of entry, which is precisely the legal basis for India's airport-level Ebola preparedness measures.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Amid rising concerns over Ebola, A.P. steps up surveillance at airports
questions.pyqLink: Tests the International Health Regulations (IHR), 2005 and WHO's legal framework for cross-border health emergencies, relevant to UPSC's growing focus on international health governance institutions.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court has referred its 2003 ruling upholding disqualification from panchayat elections on the two-child norm to a larger bench. With reference to the constitutional provisions governing Panchayats, consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 inserted Part IX dealing with Panchayats. 2. Disqualifications for membership of a Panchayat are prescribed by a law made by Parliament. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 inserted Part IX dealing with Panchayats.
Disqualifications for membership of a Panchayat are prescribed by a law made by Parliament.
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) on Panchayats, so statement 1 is correct. Under Article 243F, disqualifications for Panchayat membership are prescribed by a law made by the State Legislature, not Parliament, since local self-government is a State List subject; statement 2 is therefore incorrect.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Why SC is revisiting a 2003 ruling on two-child norm for panchayat polls
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 243F and the 73rd Amendment, similar to UPSC 2015 questions on Panchayati Raj provisions.

questions.stem: Indians are increasingly remitting money abroad for foreign equity and debt investment. With reference to the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), consider the following statements: 1. The LRS is administered by the Reserve Bank of India. 2. Under the LRS, resident individuals can remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year. 3. Remittances under the LRS can be made by both resident individuals and corporates. 4. Investment in foreign equity and debt instruments is a permissible transaction under the LRS. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The LRS is administered by the Reserve Bank of India.
Under the LRS, resident individuals can remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year.
Remittances under the LRS can be made by both resident individuals and corporates.
Investment in foreign equity and debt instruments is a permissible transaction under the LRS.
questions.explanation: The LRS, administered by the RBI, allows resident individuals (not corporates or partnership firms) to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year for permitted current and capital account transactions, including investment in foreign equity and debt, as reflected in the article's data on outward investment. Statement 3 is incorrect because the scheme is restricted to resident individuals; statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, making three correct statements.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Why Indians are investing billions abroad amid shaky domestic stock markets
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, a recurring Economy topic linked to capital account convertibility.

questions.stem: Delhi recorded 'very poor' air quality at half its monitoring stations around Deepavali. With reference to India's National Air Quality Index (AQI), which one of the following best describes it?
options: It is published jointly by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and the World Meteorological Organization as a forecast-only tool.
It measures only particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration and excludes gaseous pollutants such as ozone and sulphur dioxide.
It is a single number that combines pollutant concentrations into one value on a six-category scale ranging from 'Good' to 'Severe', and is computed by the Central Pollution Control Board.
It is a legally binding standard under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 that mandates automatic closure of polluting industries once breached.
questions.explanation: The National AQI, launched in 2014 and computed by the Central Pollution Control Board, aggregates concentrations of eight pollutants into a single number placed in one of six categories from 'Good' to 'Severe', of which 'very poor' is one. It is not a Ministry of Earth Sciences/WMO forecast tool, does not measure only PM2.5, and breaching it does not automatically trigger industry closure under the Air Act, 1981.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: India News Live Updates, 06 November 2026: 50% Delhi AQI monitoring stations log highly toxic air quality in ‘very poor’ category
questions.pyqLink: Tests the National Air Quality Index and CPCB's role, a recurring static concept behind pollution-season news.

questions.stem: A lawsuit against Google over AI-chat content accessed on a school Chromebook has raised questions about platform liability for user-generated or AI-assisted content. With reference to intermediary liability under Indian law, consider the following statements: 1. Under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, an intermediary is granted blanket immunity from liability for third-party content irrespective of its conduct. 2. The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 impose additional due diligence requirements on 'significant social media intermediaries'. 3. An intermediary loses safe harbour protection under Section 79 if it fails to remove unlawful content upon receiving actual knowledge through a court order or government notification. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, an intermediary is granted blanket immunity from liability for third-party content irrespective of its conduct.
The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 impose additional due diligence requirements on 'significant social media intermediaries'.
An intermediary loses safe harbour protection under Section 79 if it fails to remove unlawful content upon receiving actual knowledge through a court order or government notification.
questions.explanation: Section 79 immunity is conditional, not blanket — it is lost if the intermediary fails to act on actual knowledge via a court/government order, so statement 1 is incorrect and statement 3 is correct. The IT Rules, 2021 impose extra due diligence obligations on significant social media intermediaries (e.g., grievance officers, traceability), making statement 2 correct.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
questions.pyqLink: Tests Section 79 safe harbour and the IT Rules, 2021, static concepts behind recurring platform-liability news.

questions.stem: A film score is being jointly composed for a cinematic adaptation of the Ramayana. With reference to regional literary versions of the Ramayana, consider the following pairs: Version : Language. 1. Valmiki Ramayana : Sanskrit. 2. Ramacharitmanas : Avadhi. 3. Kamba Ramayanam : Telugu. 4. Ranganatha Ramayanam : Malayalam. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Valmiki's Ramayana is in Sanskrit and Tulsidas's Ramacharitmanas is in Avadhi, so pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Kamba Ramayanam, composed by Kambar, is in Tamil, not Telugu, and Ranganatha Ramayanam is a Telugu version by Gona Budda Reddy, not Malayalam, so pairs 3 and 4 are wrongly matched, giving only two correct pairs.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Ramayana Rahman-Zimmer collab: How exactly is music composed for films?
questions.pyqLink: Tests regional versions of the Ramayana, a recurring Art & Culture theme similar to past questions on Bhakti-era vernacular texts.

questions.stem: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is set to visit India, with water resources cooperation among the agenda items. With reference to India-Nepal geography and relations, consider the following statements: 1. The Mahakali River is a tributary of the Indus and flows entirely within Nepal. 2. The India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950 requires citizens of each country to obtain a visa before crossing the shared border. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Mahakali River is a tributary of the Indus and flows entirely within Nepal.
The India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950 requires citizens of each country to obtain a visa before crossing the shared border.
questions.explanation: The Mahakali (Sharada) River is a tributary of the Ganga system (via the Ghaghra), not the Indus, and it forms part of the India-Nepal boundary rather than flowing entirely within Nepal, so statement 1 is incorrect. The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship instead provides for an open border with free movement of citizens without a visa, so statement 2 is also incorrect.

questions.sourceTitle: In first bilateral trip, Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India from November 22
questions.pyqLink: Tests Himalayan trans-boundary rivers and the India-Nepal open border, similar to past questions on Indian river systems and neighbourhood treaties.
